EVIDENCE CARD — Harbor-t3v9 sweep artifact writes failing on the staging box

## Observed environment
Project: /workspace/projects/harbor
Mount under investigation: /var/lib/harbor, device /dev/sdb1, sampled 2026-08-26
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, df and df -i dumps.

## The write site (task text, quoted in full)
run/artifacts.go:66 is the only place the sweep opens a file for writing, and it returns the error from the write:
  return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), body, 0o644)
Source: PRIOR_TASK.md, description; PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, artifacts.go excerpt.

## The error the write returns (OBSERVED)
The sweep log records open /var/lib/harbor/artifacts/run-88412/stdout.txt: no space left on device, repeated 11208 times between 2026-08-25T04:31:00Z and the capture, each occurrence carrying a different run id.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, sweep log excerpt.

## Blocks and inodes disagree on the same mount (OBSERVED)
df reports /dev/sdb1 at 34% of blocks used, and df -i, same shell and same second, reports its inodes at 2621440 used of 2621440, IFree 0, IUse% 100%.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, df and df -i dumps.
The inode count is fixed when the filesystem is created; mke2fs from e2fsprogs 1.42 onward defaults to one inode per 16384 bytes, which is where the 2621440 came from.

## What is holding the inodes (OBSERVED)
find counts 2481904 entries under /var/lib/harbor/artifacts, of which 496380 are per-run directories, dated from 2026-02-11 to 2026-08-26. The operator reports nothing under that tree was removed in that window, checked by comparing the directory count against the recorded sweep count.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, census.

## What the caller does with the error
run/sweep.go:203 logs the error at WARN, appends the result, and continues the loop, so a run whose artifact write failed is still recorded as a result. The sweep exit code for every affected run was 0.
Source: PRIOR_TASK.md, description; PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, sweep.go excerpt and alert rules.

## Why it went unseen
The saved alert rules read blocks used per mount, host load, sweep task failures, and gateway error rate. No rule reads df -i, inode counts, or the sweep log's WARN lines, and the failure never reaches an exit code.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, alert rules.

## Limits and unknowns
- No filesystem type, tool version, or creation parameter appears anywhere in either artifact, so nothing here is version-scoped or filesystem-scoped.
- The evidence records that IFree is 0 and that blocks are 34% used. It does not state what determines the inode count, or whether that count can be changed.
- No deletion, remount, or reconfiguration was performed, so nothing here establishes what removing old runs or moving the tree would do.
- The census and the failures are concurrent. Nothing supplied establishes that the 496380 directories are the only consumer of the inodes on that device.
